import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Smallest prime $\equiv 1 \pmod n$

$$a(n) = \min \{p \in \mathbb{P} \mid p \equiv 1 \pmod n\}$$

*References:*
- [A034694](https://oeis.org/A034694)-/

namespace OeisA34694

/-- Smallest prime $\equiv 1 \pmod n$. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p ∧ n ∣ (p - 1)}

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 2 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 7 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 5 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 5. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 11 := IsLeast.csInf_eq <| by decide

/--
"Conjecture: $a(n) < n^2$ for $n > 1$. - _Thomas Ordowski_, Dec 19 2016"-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : a n < n ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end OeisA34694

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the natural-number infimum of primes satisfying n ∣ (p - 1), rather than explicitly taking the smallest prime congruent to 1 modulo n. The definition also accepts n = 0, outside the OEIS sequence's positive-index domain.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Primality implies p ≥ 2, so natural subtraction does not truncate and n ∣ (p - 1) is equivalent to p ≡ 1 (mod n). It is also equivalent, under primality, to the source's formula p = k*n + 1 with k > 0. For every n > 0, Nat.exists_prime_gt_modEq_one supplies a candidate, so sInf returns the actual minimum rather than its empty-set default. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved these predicate equivalences and a n = p ↔ IsLeast {q : ℕ | q.Prime ∧ q ≡ 1 [MOD n]} p for n ≠ 0. Also proved a 0 = 0; this extra value affects neither the positive-index sequence nor the conjecture, which assumes n > 1.
